title: Causal signal trellis & tracehook runtime onramp for error dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a new diagnostic surface (the 'Causal Signal Trellis') and an associated tracehook runtime onramp so we can quickly attribute inference errors to root causes (timeouts, overload, model rejects/errors, and transport codes like HTTP/gRPC). The trellis is a multi-panel visualization that cross-correlates: 1) sampled traces with span-level exit reasons, 2) token-level model error tags (e.g., generation aborted, decoding failure), 3) per-request CPU/GPU pressure signals and queue metrics, and 4) transport/HTTP/gRPC error codes and latencies. The tracehook onramp will standardize a lightweight envelope for attaching enriched metadata (exit_reason, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, queue_depth, gpu_util_bin) to traces at collection time.

Why: current dashboards are fragmented (separate latency heatmaps, error count charts, and ad-hoc trace links). Support teams need a single pane to pivot from symptom -> probable cause and to decide remediation (retry, fallback model, route to dedicated pool). This ticket scopes the initial MVP including UI, backend aggregation, tracehook spec, and a controlled rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tracehook runtime spec documented and implemented so services can emit enriched span attributes with <=1% p50 request overhead.
- Aggregation pipeline computes causal attribution slices for four primary failure classes: TIMEOUT, OVERLOAD, MODEL_ERROR, TRANSPORT_ERROR and emits normalized metrics to the dashboard backend.
- New Grafana panels: Trellis overview (failure-class distribution by service), Trace sample carousel (linked to span-level enriched traces), Queue pressure vs failures sparkline, and Top models by failure rate. Panels include per-route and per-model filters and a date range selector.
- End-to-end latency to first visualized event <= 90s for stream of synthetic load used in QA.
- Runbook stub with first-response playbook for each failure class and hooks to create postmortems.

Non-goals: deep ML model debugging (embeddings/weights), long-term storage changes, heavy-weight full-trace capture for all requests.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff sync with observability, runtime, and product. Agreed to keep tracehook envelope small (<= 5 attrs) and to use prioritized sampling for high-cost traces.

2026-02-24 - Miguel Hernandez: Prototype tracehook spec posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Tracehook+Envelope+v1.0. Attrs: exit_reason, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, queue_depth_bin, node_gpu_util_bin.

2026-03-02 - Design review: Design provided wireframes for Trellis (carousel + heat tree). Feedback: make trace samples collapsible and surface top-3 correlated metrics above trace to avoid panel noise.

2026-03-05 - Backend update (Miguel): Aggregation lambda implemented and deployed to staging. Uses prioritized sampling: all TIMEOUT/TRANSPORT_ERROR traces auto-retain, random-0.1% otherwise. Observed 0.8% p50 latency overhead on staging after initial optimizations.
2026-03-09 - QA note (Lina Xu): Synthetic load tests show overload signature correlates strongly with queue_depth_bin > 3. Need to tune queue_depth_bin thresholds for each pool type.
